$$
AB=\begin{bmatrix}2\sqrt{7} \\ -2 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}2\sqrt{7} & -3 & 3.5 \\ -2 & 2\sqrt{5} & -2.5 \\ \sqrt{3} & 4 & 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\sqrt{7}\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 0+3.5\cdot 0 \\ (-2)\cdot 1+2\sqrt{5}\cdot 0+(-2.5)\cdot 0 \\ \sqrt{3}\cdot 1+4\cdot 0+5\cdot 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\sqrt{7} \\ -2 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $3$rd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}$, the result must be the $3$rd column of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -3.5 \\ -4\sqrt{5}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

 

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{3} & -5 & 5 \\ -5 & 3\sqrt{2} & -3.5 \\ 1 & 2 & -4\sqrt{5}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{3}\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 0+5\cdot 1 \\ (-5)\cdot 0+3\sqrt{2}\cdot 0+(-3.5)\cdot 1 \\ 1\cdot 0+2\cdot 0+(-4\sqrt{5})\cdot 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -3.5 \\ -4\sqrt{5}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
